'''Oleg Alexandrovich Reutov''' (September 5, 1920 – August 15, 1998) was a [[soviet]] [[organic chemist]], Doctor of Chemical Sciences, professor at [[Moscow State University|Lomonosov Moscow State University]], Academician of the [[USSR Academy of Sciences]] (then [[Russian Academy of Sciences|RAS]]) since 1964. He was a [[Lenin Prize]] winner.

== Biography ==
He was born in [[Makeyevka]]. He graduated from secondary school No. 3 in his hometown. In 1937, he came to [[Moscow]] and entered the chemistry department of [[Lomonosov Moscow State University]].<ref name="Reutova T.O.">{{cite book |last1=Реутова Т.О. |title=Гвардеец, учёный, дипломат — фронтовые дневники академика Реутова |date=2011 |publisher=Издательский дом «Звонница-МГ» |location=М. |isbn=978-5-88093-199-6 |url=http://www.chem.msu.su/rus/books/2011/reutov/welcome.html |language=Russian |trans-title=Guardsman, scientist, diplomat — front-line diaries of Academician Reutov}}</ref>

Oleg Alexandrovich completed four courses, but he didn’t graduate from the University, because [[The Great Patriotic War]] was started and he volunteered for the front in September 1941. He participated in battles on the [[Southern Front (Soviet Union)|Southern]] and [[4th Ukrainian Front|4th Ukrainian]] fronts. He was also a member of the [[5th Tank Army]], which fought in the [[Battle of Stalingrad]]. Then in 1942 he joined [[CPSU]].<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

He had gotten rank of major and position of Deputy Head of the Chemical Division of the 4th Ukrainian Front for operational search activities. Demobilization took place in September 1945.<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

After that, Oleg Reutov returned to [[alma mater]] and became an assistant at the division of Organic Chemistry. In 1948, he defended his PhD thesis on "The study of the decomposition of arylazocarboxylic salts", conducted under the supervision of Academician [[Alexander Nesmeyanov|Alexander Nikolaevich Nesmeyanov]].<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

In 1953, Reutov defended his doctoral thesis on "The application of homolytic reactions for the synthesis of organometallic compounds".<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

For some time, he studied at the postgraduate school in philosophy with [[Bonifaty Kedrov|Bonifaty Mikhailovich Kedrov]], who later became an academician of the USSR Academy of Sciences. Reutov considered the study of philosophy extremely useful for a [[natural scientist]], especially, a deep acquaintance with [[dialectics]] was considered necessary by Oleg Alexandrovich. In his opinion, the years spent studying philosophy were repaid to him a hundredfold later in building the system of thinking of a modern scientist.<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

In 1954, he became a professor Lomonosov Moscow State University. In 1957, he founded a laboratory of theoretical problems of organic chemistry at the Division of Organic Chemistry of the Chemistry Department. This laboratory provided modern education, aimed at mastering synthetic methods and theoretical issues, and the work carried out there gained popularity soon.<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

Since 1954, Professor Reutov had been actively traveling abroad. He visited institutes of the [[GDR]], [[China]], the [[United States]], [[India]], [[Brazil]], [[Australia]], [[Japan]] and other countries.<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

Reutov was the author of the first Russian textbook "Theoretical Problems of Organic Chemistry", which was published in 1956.<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

In 1957, Oleg Alexandrovich became the head of the chemistry editorial office of [[Foreign Languages Publishing House (Soviet Union)|Foreign Languages Publishing House]] (then the publishing house "[[Mir Publishers|Mir]]").<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

Reutov’s laboratory developed a new discipline, [[physical organic chemistry]], which had not previously existed in the USSR.<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

On June 20, 1958, he was elected a Corresponding Member of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR in the specialty "Organic Chemistry, Chemistry of Labeled Atoms" (Division of Chemical Sciences).<ref name="IS ARAS"/>

In 1962, he became the Head of the Laboratory of Organic Chemistry of Isotopes at the Institute of Organoelement Compounds of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR, where research was conducted on the reaction mechanisms of organic compounds of mercury, tin, germanium, and gold.<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

On June 26, 1964, he was elected a Full Member (academician) of the USSR Academy of Sciences in the Division of General and Technical Chemistry. Soon he also took the position of academician-secretary of the Division of General and Technical Chemistry of the USSR Academy of Sciences.<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

Tatiana Voitovich in her article "High service to science" wrote:
''"Everyone who worked with Oleg Alexandrovich notes his unique ability to lead the work and the very style of this leadership. He did not limit anyone, did not impose his opinion, did not command, but he was able to guide young scientists."''<ref name="Reutova T.O."/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Войтович Т. |title=Высокое служение науке |volume=3837 |issue=2 |publisher=«Московский университет» |date=1998 |location=М. |language=Russian |trans-title=High service to science}}</ref>

Reutov developed a fundamentally new lecture course titled "Theoretical problems of organic chemistry", which he taught at the Chemistry Department for over 30 years.<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

In addition, while lecturing on Organic chemistry for 20 years, Oleg Alexandrovich took lessons from artists of the [[Maly Theatre (Moscow)|Maly Theater]] in the Central [[House of Scientists]] to maintain his voice and diction.<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

Since 1965, he was a member of the [[editorial board]] of the "Journal of Organic Chemistry" of the USSR Academy of Sciences; from 1966 to 1980, he served on the editorial board of the international abstract journal "Index Chemicus" (Philadelphia); in 1968, he became a regional editor for the international journal "Journal of Organometallic Chemistry" (Elsevier, Amsterdam).<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

Reutov was one of the academicians of the USSR Academy of Sciences who signed in 1973 a letter to the newspaper "[[Pravda]]" condemning the "behavior of Academician [[Andrei Sakharov|A.D. Sakharov]]". In the letter, Sakharov was accused of "making a series of statements discrediting the state system, foreign and domestic policy of the Soviet Union", and academicians assessed his human rights activities as "bringing dishonor and disgrace upon the Soviet scientist".<ref>{{cite news |title=Письмо членов Академии наук СССР о своем отношении к поведению академика Сахарова А.Д. |publisher=Труд |date=1973 |url=https://arch2.iofe.center/person/32739 |location=М. |language=Russian |trans-title=A letter from members of the USSR Academy of Sciences about their attitude to the behavior of Academician Sakharov A.D.}}</ref>

Since 1977, he was a member of the editorial board of the journal "Izvestiya Akademii Nauk SSSR. Seriya Khimicheskaya". In 1985, he became Chief Editor of the journal "Metalloorganic Chemistry" of the USSR Academy of Sciences.<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

From 1978 to 1993, Reutov headed the Division of Organic Chemistry at the Chemistry Department of MSU; in 1993, he became an advisor to the Rectorate of MSU, holding this position until his death.<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

He was actively involved in public life: Deputy Chairman of the [[Soviet Peace Committee|Soviet Committee for the Defense of Peace]], Deputy Chairman of the Soviet [[Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs|Pugwash Committee]] (1973–1987), and USSR expert on chemical and biological (bacteriological) warfare at the [[United Nations]].<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

O. Reutov founded a scientific school: 15 of his students became professors and Doctors of Science, and more than 150 defended their Candidate’s dissertations under his supervision. He was the author of more than 1,200 scientific papers and the holder of several patents, the list of his co-authors exceeded 400 people.<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>

He lived and worked in Moscow. He died on August 15, 1998, and was buried at the [[Novodevichy Cemetery]].<ref name="Reutova T.O."/><ref>{{cite web |title=Реутов Олег Александрович (1920-1998) |url=http://www.nd.m-necropol.ru/reutov-oa.html |website=Известные люди, похороненные на Новодевичьием кладбище. |language=Russian |date=2012 |trans-title=Oleg Aleksandrovich Reutov (1920-1998)}}</ref>

==Scientific work==
Oleg Alexandrovich Reutov was an outstanding chemist, he made a significant contribution to the development of [[organic chemistry|organic]], [[organometallic chemistry|organometallic]] and [[physical organic chemistry|physical organic]] chemistry.

In his laboratory (the laboratory of theoretical problems of organic chemistry), for the first time in the USSR, extensive investigations into the [[Reaction mechanism|mechanisms of reactions]] of organometallic [[Chemical compound|compounds]] were initiated, employing the most modern methods and concepts of physical chemistry.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Курячая М. |title=Пройдя тысячу шагов. |journal=[[Znanie – Sila|Знание — сила]] |date=1985 |issue=7 |trans-title=After walking a thousand steps. |language=Russian |issn=0130-1640}}</ref>

The beginning of Reutov's scientific career was the continuation of the study of [[diazonium]] method, proposed by his scientific supervisor, A.N. Nesmeyanov. The method was aimed at obtaining some organometallic compounds, and Oleg Alexandrovich extended this method to the synthesis of organic derivatives of [[Mercury (element)|mercury]], [[arsenic]], [[antimony]], and [[bismuth]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Реутов О.А. |last2=Птицына О.А. |title=К вопросу о синтезе сурьмяноорганических соединений методом двойных диазониевых солей |journal=Докл. АН СССР. |date=1951 |volume=79 |issue=5 |pages=819–821 |trans-title=On the question of the synthesis of organometallic antimony compounds by the method of double diazonium salts |language=Russian}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Реутов О.А. |title=Синтез ароматических мышьяковоорганических соединений через арилазокарбоновые соли |journal=Изв. АН СССР, сер. хим. |date=1952 |issue=1 |pages=93–102 |trans-title=Synthesis of aromatic organic arsenic compounds through arylazocarboxylic salts |language=Russian}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Реутов О.А. |title=Синтез ароматических висмуторганических соединений через арилазокарбоновые соли |journal=Журн. физ. химии. |date=1953 |volume=27 |issue=9 |pages=1427–1429 |trans-title=Synthesis of aromatic organic bismuth compounds through arylazocarboxylic salts |language=Russian}}</ref> He synthesized numerous novel double diazonium salts and conducted extensive research on mechanisms of these complex reactions. The logical continuation of his studies on diazonium salt chemistry led him into the field of [[Onium ion|onium]] compounds, particularly iodonium compounds. New methods for synthesizing mercury-, [[tin]]-, antimony-, and bismuth-organic compounds were developed. For the first time, salts of diaryliodonium with [[Isotopic labeling|labeled]] [[iodine]] were synthesized.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Реутов О. А. |last2=Птицына О. А. |last3=Ху Хун-вен |title=Синтез ртутьорганических соединений через соли диарилиодония |journal=Докл. АН СССР. |date=1958 |volume=122 |issue=5 |pages=825–827 |trans-title=Synthesis of organosilver compounds through diaryliodonium salts |language=Russian}}</ref>

Reutov was the first to insert mono- and [[Carbene|dihalocarbenes]] (in particular, [[dichlorocarbene]]) across mercury-[[halogen]] [[Chemical bond|bond]], obtaining asymmetric mercury derivatives that contained a trichloromethyl group (R-Hg-Cl + :CCl2 = R-Hg-CCl3). Such substances long served as the best source of dichlorocarbenes and were termed "preserved carbenes".<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Реутов О. А. |last2=Ловцова А. Н. |title=Внедрение дихлоркарбена по связи металл-галоид |journal=Изв. АН СССР. ОХН. |date=1960 |issue=9 |pages=1716–1717 |trans-title=Insertion of dichlorocarbene into metal-halide bond |language=Russian}}</ref>

Reutov was also one of the first to use labeled atoms to study the mechanisms of organic reactions, i.e. [[Isotopes of mercury|<sup>203</sup>Hg]] was used to study exchange between metallic mercury and diarylmercury and [[Carbon-14|<sup>14</sup>C]] was used to investigate [[Rearrangement reaction|rearrangements]] in [[Alkyl group|alkyl]] [[Radical (chemistry)|radicals]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Спицын В.И. |title=Изотопы в науных исследованиях. |journal=Атомная энергия. |date=1969 |volume=26 |issue=2 |pages=114–122 |url=https://elib.biblioatom.ru/text/atomnaya-energiya_t26-2_1969/p122/ |trans-title=Isotopes in scientific research. |language=Russian}}</ref>

An important part of Reutov's research work was a series of experiments conducted with many members of his laboratory on [[electrophilic substitution]] at saturated [[carbon]] atom.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Реутов О.А. |last2=Несмеянов А. Н. |title=К вопросу о механизме реакций электрофильного замещения у насыщенного углеродного атома. |journal=Докл. к Всесоюз. совещ. по хим. кинетике и реакцион. способности. |date=1955 |pages=739–748 |trans-title=On the mechanism of electrophilic substitution reactions in saturated carbon atoms |language=Russian}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Реутов О. А. |last2=Белецкая И. П. |last3=Мардалейшвили Р. Е. |title=Кинетика реакции электрофильного замещения у насыщенного атома углерода. |journal=Докл. АН СССР. |date=1957 |volume=116 |issue=4 |pages=617–620 |trans-title=Kinetics of electrophilic substitution reaction in saturated carbon atom |language=Russian}}</ref> These works led to the discovery of a new mechanism of electrophilic substitution, S<sub>E</sub>1, wherein the rate-limiting step involves dissociation or ionization of an organometallic compound, followed by a rapid step in which the resulting [[carbanion]] or its ion pair interacts with an [[electrophilic]] agent. Subsequently, in the 1970s, intermediate cases between S<sub>E</sub>1 and S<sub>E</sub>2 mechanisms were identified – the ion-pair mechanism of bimolecular electrophilic substitution, in which ionization of the organometallic compound occurs in a pre-equilibrium step, followed by attack of the electrophilic agent on the ion pair in the rate-limiting step.<ref name="Beletskaya I.P. (1985)">{{cite journal |last1=Beletskaya I.P. |title=he scientific contribution by professor O.A.Reutov to organometallic chemistry. |journal=J. Organomet. Chem. |date=1985 |volume=292 |issue=1 |doi=10.1016/0022-328x(85)87313-7}}</ref>

Based on polarographic data obtained by O. A. Reutov, a polarographic scale of acidity for CH-acids was constructed. This scale enabled characterization of CH-acids differing by nearly 60 pKa units and determination of the acidity of specific C–H bonds within molecules.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Реутов О.А. |title=Полярография ртутноорганических соединений. Этиловый эфир α-броммеркурфенилуксусной кислоты и его замещение. |journal=Журн. орган. хим. |date=1967 |volume=3 |issue=2 |page=231 |trans-title=Polarography of organosilver compounds. Ethyl ether of α-brommercurphenylacetic acid and its substitution. |language=Russian}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Реутов О.А. |title=Полярография диарилгалогенониевых солей. |journal=Докл. АН СССР. |date=1971 |volume=201 |issue=2 |pages=372–374 |trans-title=Polarography of diarylhalogenonium salts |language=Russian}}</ref>

Parallel to his studies of electrophilic substitution reactions in organomercury compounds, Reutov discovered and investigated reactions proceeding by a [[Homolysis (chemistry)|homolytic]] mechanisms.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Кузьменко Р. И. |last2=Финашина Г. Н. |title=Олег Александрович Реутов. (Материалы к библиографии учёных. Серия химических наук.) |date=1992 |publisher=Наука |location=M. |isbn=5-02-001604-7 |pages=10–23 |edition=2 |language=Russian |trans-title=Oleg Alexandrovich Reutov. (Materials for the bibliography of scientists. A series of chemical sciences.)}}</ref>

Reutov and his students conducted a series of studies on the mechanism of [[nucleophilic aromatic substitution]] and on anionic [[Sigma complex|σ-complexes]] as possible [[intermediate (chemistry)|intermediates]] in these reactions.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Реутов О. А. |title=Электрофильное замещение у ароматического атома углерода. |journal=Журн. орган. химии. |date=1966 |volume=2 |issue=12 |pages=2086–2093 |trans-title=Electrophilic substitution of aromatic carbon atom |language=Russian}}</ref> They synthesized novel anionic σ-complexes of [[trinitrobenzene]] with C–E bonds in [[geminal]] positions (E = Si, Ge, Sn) and studied their transformation pathways in solution. A new rearrangement of these σ-complexes into [[nitrophenol|3,5-dinitrophenols]] was discovered.

A separate research cycle by O. A. Reutov was dedicated to the chemistry of arsenic and [[phosphorus]] [[ylides]]. Of particular interest was the synthesis of novel arsenic derivatives and the comparison of properties of arsenic and phosphorus ylides.<ref name="Beletskaya I.P. (1985)"/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Реутов О. А. |last2=Несмеянов Н. А. |last3=Берман С. Т. |title=Взаимодействие илидов фосфора с перфторбензолом. |journal=Изв. АН СССР. Сер. хим. |date=1972 |issue=3 |pages=605–606 |trans-title=Interaction of phosphorus ylides with perfluorobenzene |language=Russian}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Реутов О.А. |last2=Несмеянов Н.А. |last3=Биншток Е.В. |title=Механизм реакций стабильных илидов мышьяка с альдегидами. |date=1971 |volume=2 |pages=78–81 |trans-title=Mechanism of reactions of stable arsenic ylides with aldehydes |journal=V Международный конгресс по металлоорганической химии: Тез. докл. |location=Москва |language=Russian}}</ref>

O. A. Reutov initiated a series of studies on the [[metal complexes]], conducted using low-temperature [[NMR spectroscopy]] of heavy nuclei.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=PETROSYAN V.S. |last2=Reutov O.A. |title=STUDY OF THE STRUCTURE AND COMPLEXATION OF ORGANIC AND INORGANIC DERIVATIVES OF METALS BY MEANS OF N.M.R. SPECTROSCOPY OF HEAVY NUCLEI |journal=Molecular Spectroscopy–XI |date=1974 |pages=147–159 |doi=10.1016/B978-0-408-70635-3.50012-X}}</ref> Later, he investigated dynamic changes in metal complexes with unsaturated carbon-carbon bound and [[aromatic]] ligands.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Galakhov M.V. |last2=Bakhmutov V.I. |last3=Barinov I.V. |last4=Reutov O.A. |title=<sup>1</sup>H and <sup>13</sup>C NMR study of low-energy intramolecular transformations of coordinated propargyl cations [(μ-η<sup>2</sup>-η<sup>3</sup>-HCCCR<sub>1</sub>R<sub>2</sub>)Cp<sub>2</sub>Mo<sub>2</sub>(CO)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>+</sup>BF<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup> |journal=Journal of Organometallic Chemistry |date=1991 |volume=421 |issue=1 |pages=65–73 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0022328X9186432P}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Krut'ko D.P. |last2=Borzov M.V. |last3=Churakov A.V. |last4=Lemenovśkii  D.A. |last5=Reutov O.A. |title=Synthesis and photoinduced isomerization ofansa{·<sup>5</sup>,·<sup>5</sup>′-[1,1′-(1-silacyclopent-3-ene-1,1-diyl)bis(indenyl)]} dichlorozirconium The crystal structure of its meso form. |journal=Russian Chemical Bulletin |date=1998 |volume=47 |pages=2280–2285 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF02494296#citeas}}</ref>

==Awards==
The list of awards is mainly taken from the book by T. Reutova.<ref name="Reutova T.O."/>
* [[Medal "For the Defence of Stalingrad"|Medal "For the Defense of Stalingrad"]] (1942)
* Medal "For Combat Merits" (April 29, 1943)<ref name="EDB">{{cite web |title=Реутов Олег Александрович 1920г.р. |url=https://podvignaroda.ru/?#id=1003952924&tab=navDetailManCard |website=ЭЛЕКТРОННЫЙ БАНК ДОКУМЕНТОВ «ПОДВИГ НАРОДА В ВЕЛИКОЙ ОТЕЧЕСТВЕННОЙ ВОЙНЕ 1941-1945 ГГ.» |language=Russian |trans-title=Oleg Aleksandrovich Reutov (1920-1998)}}</ref>
* [[Order of the Red Star]] (May 17, 1944)<ref name="EDB"/>
* Two [[Orders of the Patriotic War]], 2nd Class (November 6, 1944;<ref name="EDB"/> March 11, 1985)
* Order of the Patriotic War, 1st Class (June 3, 1945)<ref name="EDB"/>
* Medal "For Victory over Germany in the Great Patriotic War 1941—1945" (1945)
* M. V. Lomonosov Prize, 1st Class (1956) – for the research cycle on the mechanism of synthesis of organometallic compounds via diazo compounds
* A. M. Butlerov Prize of the Presidium of the USSR Academy of Sciences (1961) – for a series of works in the field of organomercury compounds
* Two [[Order of the Red Banner of Labour]] (1961 – for outstanding contributions to training specialists and developing science; October 2, 1970 – for outstanding contributions to the development of chemical science, fruitful scientific and pedagogical activity, and in connection with his 50th birthday)
* [[Order of the October Revolution]] (September 17, 1975) – for contributions to the development of Soviet science and in connection with the 250th anniversary of the USSR Academy of Sciences
* [[Order of Lenin]] (September 4, 1980) – for outstanding contributions to the development of chemical science, training of scientific personnel, and in connection with his 60th birthday
* [[Lenin Prize]] (1984) – for the research cycle "Studies in the Field of Organometallic Chemistry of Non-transition Metals"
